question: Why is it sufficient, when estimating the difference between Riemann sums of a refinement, to consider only the norm of the coarser partition?
answer: A refinement subdivides the intervals of the coarser partition, so every subinterval in the refinement is contained in some interval of the coarser partition. Therefore the largest subinterval length in the refinement cannot exceed the norm of the coarser partition. The modulus of continuity evaluated at that norm controls the maximum change in \(F\) on any subinterval, making it sufficient for bounding the difference between the two Riemann sums.
